ov: The widow spiders: 34 species of small spiders with unusually potent venom. Females are usually shiny black with a red or orange hourglass on the underside. They hang upside down in tangled webs, and the name comes from females sometimes eating the male after mating.

why.dg: Only females’ bites are dangerous, and they rarely cause death; the US recorded no black widow deaths from 1983 to 2012.

len: Body 3–10 mm; females 25–38 mm including legs
rg: Worldwide: North America, Europe, Australia (redback), New Zealand (katipō), southern Africa and South America.
fx: Much of the evidence for males being eaten comes from lab cages, where the males could not escape.
A trapped widow is more likely to play dead or flick silk than to bite.
